description:
FILED s450t (Opus, agent T of round 8).  Named as a separate task by the
ruled design, docs/computed-magic-design-s449.md SS4 last bullet, on rule 9a:
`%!` itself is CORE (perl auto-loads Errno for it; PCL just defines it, done
in #561), but `use POSIX qw(ENOENT)` / `use Errno qw(ENOENT)` and
`Errno::ENOENT()` are one MODULE's exports and belong in a shim.

SHAPE: lib/Errno.pm declares each constant as a zero-prototype sub reading
the ONE runtime table *p-errno-table* through a single builtin (the
`builtin::` seam is blessed for exactly this -- docs/DECIDED.md s377), so the
name list is not duplicated.  @EXPORT_OK is every name in the table, and
`use Errno;` exports nothing by default (perl exports on request only --
PROBE this before writing it).

DO NOT hardcode a second name list: the runtime table is the source, and a
shim with its own copy is the drift #561's comment warns about.

BAR: `use Errno qw(ENOENT); print ENOENT;` and `Errno::EACCES()` vs perl;
`$!{ENOENT}` unaffected; a row in the errno guard set
(Pl/t/errno-magic-01.t).
subject: lib/Errno.pm shim: export the errno constants over the runtime's *p-errno-table* (the #561 design's named follow-on, module layer)
